speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease.

Given the patient's age (18 months), insidious onset of right knee swelling without trauma, and a strong family history of similar orthopedic issues, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of idiopathic avascular necrosis of the femoral head. I am requesting a diagnostic image to confirm. REQUEST IMAGES: Radiograph of the right knee and hip.
